sections.skill: Estimate affordable rent and prepare a rental application

questions.prompt: A common guideline suggests spending no more than 30% of gross monthly income on rent. Mo earns $3,200 a month before taxes. What is the most rent under that guideline?
questions.intro: A common affordability guideline: rent of no more than about 30% of gross (before-tax) monthly income. It is a rule of thumb, not a law; your full budget matters too.
sources: HUD (Fair Housing Act): The Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. (https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp/fair_housing_act_overview)

questions.prompt: Some landlords require yearly gross income of at least 40 times the monthly rent. Rent is $1,200. What yearly income is required?
questions.intro: Landlords often set income requirements, such as "yearly income at least 40× the monthly rent" or "monthly income at least 3× the rent."
sources: HUD (Fair Housing Act): The Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. (https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp/fair_housing_act_overview)

questions.prompt: Mo earns $36,000 a year. Under a "40 times the rent" rule, what is the highest rent he qualifies for?
questions.intro: To find the maximum rent under an income rule, divide yearly income by the multiple.
sources: HUD (Fair Housing Act): The Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. (https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp/fair_housing_act_overview)

questions.prompt: Which documents does a rental application commonly ask for?

choices.text: A high school diploma and report cards
ID, proof of income, rental history, and credit consent
A car title and insurance card
A list of friends' phone numbers

questions.correct_answer: ID, proof of income, rental history, and credit consent
questions.intro: Applications usually require photo ID, proof of income (pay stubs or an offer letter), past landlord references, and consent to a credit and background check. An application fee is common.
questions.feedback: Landlords verify identity, income, history, and credit.
sources: HUD (Fair Housing Act): The Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. (https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp/fair_housing_act_overview)

questions.prompt: Mo has no rental history and a thin credit file. What might a landlord ask for?

choices.text: Nothing; landlords cannot ask for anything else
Proof that he has never borrowed money
His Social Security card mailed in
A guarantor (cosigner) or a larger deposit, where legal

questions.correct_answer: A guarantor (cosigner) or a larger deposit, where legal
questions.intro: A guarantor agrees to pay the rent if the tenant does not. Deposit limits depend on state law.
questions.feedback: Guarantors (or deposits within legal limits) reduce the landlord's risk.
sources: HUD (Fair Housing Act): The Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. (https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp/fair_housing_act_overview)

sections.relationship: Affordability rules are percents and multiples of income.

questions.prompt: Yearly income is $33,600. Dividing by 40 gives what monthly rent limit?
questions.intro: Under a "40 times rent" rule, the most rent = yearly income ÷ 40.

questions.prompt: A common rule of thumb flags spending more than 30% of income on rent. Why does that matter?

choices.text: Less money remains for other needs and saving
Landlords charge more to such tenants
It lowers credit scores automatically each month
It is illegal to rent above 30%

questions.correct_answer: Less money remains for other needs and saving
questions.intro: The 30% rent rule of thumb is a quick budgeting check. The government's formal "cost-burdened" measure counts total housing costs, including utilities, above 30% of income.
questions.feedback: High housing costs crowd out other needs and saving.

questions.prompt: Move-in costs: first month's rent $1,000, security deposit $1,500, and a $50 application fee. How much cash does Mo need?
questions.intro: Move-in costs often include first month's rent, a security deposit, fees, and moving expenses, all due before or at move-in.
sources: HUD (Fair Housing Act): The Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. (https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp/fair_housing_act_overview)

questions.prompt: Mo saves $300 a month toward $2,550 of move-in costs. How many months until he has enough (rounded up)?

choices.text: 9 months
8 months
85 months
3 months

questions.intro: Months needed = amount needed ÷ monthly saving, rounded up to a whole month.
sources: HUD (Fair Housing Act): The Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. (https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp/fair_housing_act_overview)

questions.prompt: Which expense is often forgotten in a first apartment budget?

choices.text: Rent
The lease itself
Rent for the first month, which the landlord already listed
Furniture, kitchen supplies, and utility setup fees

questions.correct_answer: Furniture, kitchen supplies, and utility setup fees
questions.intro: First apartments often need furniture, kitchen basics, and utility deposits or setup fees.
questions.feedback: One-time setup costs can be large.
sources: HUD (Fair Housing Act): The Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. (https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp/fair_housing_act_overview)

questions.prompt: Mo's take-home pay is $2,500. Rent is $900, utilities $120, renters insurance $15, and internet $50. What share of take-home pay do these housing costs use (nearest whole percent)?
questions.intro: Housing share = total housing costs ÷ income × 100.
sources: HUD (Fair Housing Act): The Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. (https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp/fair_housing_act_overview)

questions.prompt: Which choice would most lower Mo's housing share?

choices.text: Adding cable TV
Finding a roommate to split rent and utilities
Taking a bigger unit so a future roommate can join later
Paying rent with a credit card

questions.correct_answer: Finding a roommate to split rent and utilities
questions.feedback: Splitting fixed costs is one of the biggest savings available.

questions.prompt: A landlord runs a credit check on Mo. Does this affect his credit score?

choices.text: It erases his credit history
It always drops his score by 100 points
It may appear as an inquiry; it does not reveal income
It shows his bank balances and pay to the landlord directly

questions.correct_answer: It may appear as an inquiry; it does not reveal income
questions.intro: Landlords may check credit reports (with permission). Some checks are recorded as inquiries.
questions.feedback: Tenant screening may add an inquiry; reports do not show income or bank balances.
sources: HUD (Fair Housing Act): The Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. (https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp/fair_housing_act_overview)

questions.prompt: A landlord refuses to rent to a family because they have young children. Under the federal Fair Housing Act, this is…

choices.text: legal in every building
illegal discrimination based on familial status
allowed whenever the landlord prefers a quiet building
required by fire codes

questions.correct_answer: illegal discrimination based on familial status
questions.intro: The Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. Some exemptions exist, such as certain senior housing.
questions.feedback: Familial status is a protected class under the Fair Housing Act.
sources: HUD (Fair Housing Act): The Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. (https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp/fair_housing_act_overview)

questions.prompt: Where can someone report housing discrimination?

choices.text: The IRS
The credit bureau that reported his score
HUD or the state civil rights agency
The landlord's friend

questions.correct_answer: HUD or the state civil rights agency
questions.intro: HUD and state agencies enforce fair housing laws.
questions.feedback: HUD and state agencies accept fair housing complaints.

questions.prompt: A landlord denies Mo because of information in a tenant screening report. What right does Mo have under federal law?

choices.text: None at all
To have the landlord approve him anyway
To sue the landlord for checking
To be told and to get a free copy to dispute errors

questions.correct_answer: To be told and to get a free copy to dispute errors
questions.intro: When a landlord takes adverse action based on a consumer report, the applicant must be told and can get a free copy of the report.
questions.feedback: Adverse action notices let applicants check and dispute reports.
